शम्ब् cl. 1. P. शम्बति, to go, Dhātup. xi, 29 (Vop.);
 cl. 10. P. शम्बयति, to collect, ib. xxxii, 21 (v.l.)
सम्ब्, सम्ब &c. See √ शम्ब्, p. 1055.
साम्ब् v.l. for √ सम्ब्, q.v., p. 1177.
श॑म्ब m. (derivation doubtful) a weapon used by Indra (accord. to some ‘Indra's thunderbolt’, but cf. शम्बि॑न्), RV. x, 42, 7 (= वज्र, Naigh. iv, 2)
the iron head of a pestle, L.
an iron chain worn round the loins, W.
a partic. measure of length, L.
ploughing in the regular direction (= अनुलोम-कर्षण), L.
the second ploughing of a field, W.
N. of an Asura (cf. शम्बर), TBr., Sch.
श॑म्ब mfn. happy, fortunate, L. (cf. शं-वत्, p. 1054, col. 2)
poor (?), L.
शाम्ब m. N. of a king, Daś. (also w.r. for साम्ब, q.v.)

1. साम्ब m. (also written शाम्ब) N. of a son of Kṛṣṇa and Jāmbavatī (in consequence of the curse of some holy sages who had been deceived by a female disguise which he had assumed, he was condemned to produce offspring in the shape of a terrific iron club for the destruction of the race of Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka; he is said to have been instructed by Nārada in the worship of the sun, and by Vyāsa in the ritual of the Magi), MBh.; Hariv.; Pur.
(also with शास्त्रिन्) N. of various authors and teachers, Cat.
साम्ब n. = -पुराण, ib.
2. साम्ब mfn. attended by Ambā (q.v.), KāśīKh.

श॑म्बर m. N. of a demon (in RV. often mentioned with Śuṣṇa, Arbuda, Pipru &c.; he is the chief enemy of Divo-dāsa Atithigva, for whose deliverance he was thrown down a mountain and slain by Indra; in epic and later poetry he is also a foe of the god of love), RV. &c. &c.
a cloud, Naigh. i, 10
a weapon, Sāy. on RV. i, 112, 14
war, fight, L.
a kind of deer, Vās.; Bhpr.
a fish or a kind of fish, L.
Terminalia Arunja, L.
Symplocos Racemosa, L.
a mountain in general or a partic. mountain, L.
best, excellent, L.
= चित्रक, L.
N. of of a Jina, L.
of a king, Vās. (v.l. for शम्बरण and सं-वरण)
of a juggler (also called शम्बरसिद्धि), Ratnāv.
श॑म्बर n. water, Naigh. i, 12 (but, Sāh. censures the use of शम्बर in this sense)
power, might, Naigh. ii, 9
sorcery, magic, Kathās. (printed सं-वर)
any vow or a partic. vow (with Buddhists), L.
wealth, L.
= चित्र, L.
(pl.) the fastnesses of Śambara, RV.
शाम्बर॑ mf(ई॑)n. relating or belonging or peculiar to Śambara, RV.; Hariv. &c.
coming from the deer called Ś˚, Bhpr.
शाम्बर॑ n. the fight with Ś˚, RV.
a kind of sandal, L. (cf. शाबर).
सम्बर v.l. for शम्बर, सं-वर, and सम्-भर (qq.vv.)
साम्बर, ˚री. See शाम्ब् p. 1065.
श॑म्बरी (ई), f. Salvinia Cucullata, L.; Croton Polyandrum, L.
= माया, sorcery, magic (prob. w.r. for शाम्बरी), L.
शाम्बरी॑ (ई), f. jugglery, sorcery, illusion (as practised by the Daitya Ś˚), Naiṣ.
a sorceress, W.
शम्बर—कन्द m. a kind of bulbous plant, L.
शम्बर—घ्न m. ‘Sambara-slayer’, N. of the god of love, Hariv.
शम्बर—चन्दन n. a variety of sandal, L.
शम्बर—दारण m. ‘Śambara -destoyer’, the god of love, Gīt.
शम्बर—रिपु m. ‘enemy of S˚’ id., Bhām.
शम्बर—वृत्र-हन् m. ‘slayer of S˚ and Vṛtra’, N. of Indra, R.

शम्बर—सूदन m. ‘destroyer of Ś˚’, the god of love, L.,
शम्बर—ह॑त्य n. the killing of Ś˚, RV.; TBr.; ŚāṅkhŚr.

शम्बरारि m. enemy of Ś˚, Hāsy.

envy, jealousy, L.
सम्बल See शम्बल, p. 1055.

a snail, W.
a kind of animal (= घोङ्घ), L.
the edge of the frontal protuberance of an elephant, L.
N. of a Śūdra (who had become a devotee and was slain by Rāma-candra), R.; Uttarar. (cf. शम्बुक)
of a Daitya, L.
शाम्बुक m. a bivalve shell, W.
शाम्बूक m. = शाम्बुक, L.
शम्बूक—पुष्पी f. a species of plant (= सङ्ख-प्˚), Bhpr.

a relation, relative, kinsman, fellow, friend, ally, Āpast.; MBh.; BhP.
a collection, volume, book, Śukas.
a partic. kind of calamity, VarBṛS.
prosperity, success, L.
fitness, propriety, L.
the application of authority to prove a theological doctrine, W.
सम्-बन्ध mfn. able, capable, L.
fit, right, proper, L.
(ifc.) often w.r. for सम्-बद्ध (q.v.)
